decisions.rationale: The first and last utterances align exclusively to the same run-scoped MOSS speaker S01 and bracket the intervening S02 turn. Their timing and the stopwatch-coordination context support one recurring participant despite the short voice_3 sample receiving a below-threshold TST comparison to voice_0.

TST treated this speech as a distinct voice after rejecting voice_0. Its broad interval ambiguously overlaps both S01 and S02 in MOSS, so preserving the existing unnamed identity associated with voice_1 is more supported than merging it with either neighboring speaker.

TST rejected both earlier voices and established voice_2 as distinct. Although its boundary overlaps adjacent S02 and S01 MOSS segments, there is insufficient evidence to merge it with either, so the existing unnamed person associated with voice_2 is the likeliest default.
The memory explicitly refers to voice_0, assigned to person_0.
The memory explicitly refers to voice_1, whose distinct native identity is retained as person_1.
The memory explicitly refers to voice_2, assigned to person_2.
The memory explicitly refers to voice_3, which is consolidated with the recurring S01 participant represented by person_0.
